title: Bologna court rules Deliveroo's rider-ranking algorithm discriminatory
description: The Tribunale di Bologna ruled on 31 December 2020 that Deliveroo Italy's rider-booking algorithm, known as 'Frank,' was discriminatory under Italian anti-discrimination law because it penalised any rider absence from a booked shift — whether due to illness, a technical problem, or participation in a strike — with the same reduction in 'reliability' score, without distinguishing legally-protected reasons for non-attendance from unjustified ones. The case was brought by three CGIL union federations against Deliveroo Italia S.r.l.; the court ordered Deliveroo to pay damages plus legal costs and to publish the ruling.

history.note: Initial Edition 1.1 content. The case is procedurally a collective anti-discrimination action (Article 28 of Legislative Decree 150/2011), not a full-trial-stage judgment on the employment relationship itself; secondary sources use 'ruling'/'sentenza' loosely.

root_cause: The algorithm scored and penalised rider absences uniformly, treating all non-attendance (trivial, health-related, or strike-related) as an equivalent negative signal, without any mechanism to distinguish legally protected non-performance from unjustified non-performance.

citations.title: Sentenza Tribunale di Bologna, R.G. 2949/2019 (Sezione Lavoro)
Italian court rules against 'discriminatory' Deliveroo rider-ranking algorithm

relationships.reason: Requiring the algorithm to distinguish protected absences from unjustified ones, with a human-reviewable appeal, addresses exactly the discrimination this ruling found.
This ruling, alongside the Uber Amsterdam case, established the EU legal pattern this board question addresses.
